newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares seen drifting lower until rates cut.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares seen drifting lower until rates cut.

text.p: Philippine shares fell sharply on Thursday and are set for further declines unless peso concerns ease and high interest rates are cut, analysts said.
Foreign selling hammered the main index to a two-week low. It lost 63.57 points, or 2.41 percent, to close at 2,572.80.
"People are disappointed because they were expecting rates to be cut. Everyone's holding off any positioning until rates are lowered," said Cilette Liboro, research head at Orion-Squire Capital.

The central bank had promised to reduce overnight rates further as the peso stabilised. However, it has not done so since last Friday when the overnight borrowing rate was cut to 25 percent from 27 percent.

"I think some quarters are feeling apprehensive about interest rates staying at high levels, longer than what most people expected. It's not conducive to good corporate profits," said Nathan Lozada, assistant vice-president at Paribas Asia Equity.

Renewed concerns about the peso after the Thai baht fell to a new low on Wednesday morning also kept market players sidelined, analysts said. The peso, which was effectively devalued over a week ago, had fallen prey in recent months to speculation caused by Thailand's financial woes.

"I hate to be so negative but since there was an attack on the baht this morning, there's a possibility that there may be one on the peso. People are looking at the region as a whole and the Philippines as part of it," said Liboro.
Losing stocks trounced gainers 119 to 22 in the broad market on Thursday with foreign selling hitting blue-chip Manila Electric Corp B and Ayala Land Inc.

One foreign trader said stronger first-half earnings may bring back some cheer into the market but this could take time as investors await the release of more corporate earnings and a clearer trend is established.

"The number of losers today is clear evidence that the bear power is there. We can expect major turbulence in the coming days. The worst is yet to come," said Jonathan Ravelas, head of sales at Asian Capital Equities.
Traders said any rallies would be technical and short-term with resistance at 2,650 points.
